newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia sets July 25 for Svyazinvest sale -Interfax.
newsitem.headline: Russia sets July 25 for Svyazinvest sale -Interfax.

text.p: Russia will hold an auction of a 25 percent plus one share stake in telecoms holding company AO Svyazinvest on July 25, Interfax news agency said on Saturday.
Quoting the Russian Federal Property Fund, which is responsible for the sale of state property, Interfax said applications to participate in the auction would be accepted from June 23 until July 21.
More than 4.8 billion shares, each with a nominal value of 1,000 roubles, would be offered as a single tranche. The starting value of the stake is $1.18 billion.
The potential participants in the auction must pay a deposit of 2.32 trillion roubles or $400 million by July 21, Interfax said.

The winner of the auction would be the participant which offered the highest price for the purchase of Svyazinvest's stake. If two or more participants offered the same price the winner would be the one which paid its deposit first, it added.
The deposit would be included as part of the price of the stake. Half of the final price agreed for the shares must be paid within 15 days of the deal being agreed and the remainder within 75 days.
The federal government would receive 71 percent of the proceeds of the sale, which the Fund expected to be not less than four trillion roubles, Interfax said.
The government's need to plug a huge budget deficit has given a fresh impetus to its plans to sell the Svyazinvest stake, which has been delayed for two years.

On Friday Fund spokesman Vladimir Yefimchik told Reuters that Deputy Prime Minister Alfred Kokh had approved the order for selling the 25 percent plus one ordinary share stake, but declined to give details of the auction.
The auction, which will be open to both Russian and foreign investors, was due to be announced on June 10, but has been repeatedly delayed to allow amendments to the conditions.
Svyazinvest, one of Russia's biggest companies, owns controlling stakes in 85 regional telecoms companies.
